text:
Columbus beat Buffalo 6-3 on Oct. 1. The rematch was settled in one stretch of the second period, and Josh Norris was in the middle of it.

The first was even enough. Jack Quinn scored on a backhand at 6:50, Kent Johnson tied it at 16:00, and Norris restored the lead at 18:10 with Owen Power picking up the assist. The Sabres had the better chances, 1.34 expected goals to 0.80 (expected goals measure the quality of the looks a team gets), but it was a one-goal game.

Then the second period happened. Rasmus Dahlin scored from the point at 4:30 on a slap shot given a 3% chance. Norris added his second at 9:46 on a backhand, set up by Zach Benson and Tage Thompson, and Josh Doan redirected one at 10:53 to make it 5-1. Buffalo more than doubled Columbus on expected goals in that period, and the game was effectively over before the second intermission.

Norris played only 13 minutes and the Blue Jackets created almost nothing against him: 0.09 expected goals with him on the ice. Power had three assists. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 24 of 26 and saved about 1.1 goals more than his shots deserved; his biggest stop came in the third, on a 49% chance for Mathieu Olivier, which would have made the last 20 minutes a lot more interesting. Jet Greaves faced 37 shots at the other end and gave up five.

Columbus did win the third on chances, 1.38 to 0.60, and Zach Werenski got a power-play goal at 18:21, but that is what trailing teams do against a team sitting on a lead. Over the full game Buffalo deserved to win 65% of the time (the share of replays of every shot that the Sabres win). The one blemish for Buffalo is a power play that went 0 for 4. For Columbus, Johnson had a goal, an assist and five shots, and the night still slipped away in one bad stretch.
headline: Norris scores twice as the Sabres pull away early
